images.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar as a Barrister at the London School of Economics
images.description: Studio portrait of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar dressed in formal barrister's robes and a wig.
images.historical_context: Dr. Ambedkar was called to the Bar at Gray's Inn and completed his studies at the London School of Economics. This 1922 photograph documents his formal entry into the legal profession in the United Kingdom before his return to India, where he would go on to practice at the Bombay High Court.

images.title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar at the Second Round Table Conference
images.description: A wide group photograph of delegates seated at a large table. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is seated fourth from the left in the foreground, with Mahatma Gandhi and British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald seated in the center background.
images.historical_context: In October 1931, Dr. Ambedkar represented the 'Depressed Classes' at the Second Round Table Conference in London. This conference was a pivotal historical moment where Ambedkar fiercely debated Mahatma Gandhi, arguing for separate electorates to secure political representation and basic rights for untouchables.

event.description: Constitutional reform discussions regarding the future of British India.

images.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar with his family members at Rajgruha
images.description: A group photograph taken outdoors. From left to right: Yashwant (Son), Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Smt. Ramabai (Wife), Smt. Laxmibai (Sister-in-law), alongside a dog named Tobby.
images.historical_context: Taken in February 1934, this is a rare, fully documented family photograph at Rajgruha, his custom-built residence in the Hindu Colony, Dadar (Bombay). It shows Ambedkar with his first wife, Ramabai, whose sacrifices heavily supported his early career, just a year before her passing in 1935.
